coverage: Source-listed wartime and recovery records with separate crosschecked and single-source evidence; see season coverage notes.

coverageNotes.text: Albion did not enter wartime regional league competitions. This does not claim that no friendlies were played. The club’s account explains its refusal to join in 1918 and the return in March 1919.

All six Midland Victory League fixtures are included: four original crosschecked records and two single-source additions (Derby away 12 April and Villa home 19 April). W3 D1 L2 GF12 GA5 agrees with RSSSF; aggregate agreement is not individual match corroboration. This was post-armistice football before the national league resumed.

All 42 Football League South fixtures are now represented: the original 14 crosschecked records plus 28 labelled single-source additions in wartime-1945-46-research.json. The restarted FA Cup is official competitive football and stays outside this wartime ledger. The regional league continued wartime arrangements after the war.

No openly licensed comprehensive reusable WWI or 1945/46 match-level dataset located. Individual dates and scores were reconciled across named sources. Club 1919 article prints goal average 2.00, inconsistent with RSSSF and the six results (12/5=2.4); do not repeat its arithmetic. Scorers and attendance were not imported.

coverageNotes: The original WWII cohort contains 36 corroborated fixtures: 14 in 1939/40, 6 in 1941/42, 4 in 1942/43, 8 in 1943/44 and 4 in 1944/45. The 1940/41 additions are retained in wartime-1940-41-research.json. The 1941/42 additions are retained in wartime-1941-42-research.json. The 1942/43 additions are retained in wartime-1942-43-research.json. The 1943/44 additions are retained in wartime-1943-44-research.json. The 1944/45 additions are retained in wartime-1944-45-research.json. The 1939/40 additions are retained in wartime-1939-40-research.json.

The original 1939/40 Football League War Cup campaign is complete: six matches. The full reported 1943/44 Midland Cup campaign is now included through the separate season file; both final legs retain their crosschecked evidence.

These are factual result entries with source links, not copied prose, line-ups, scorers or full source tables. No blanket reuse licence was found for Albion Till We Die, Wolves Complete History, The City Ground or Blue Correspondent; this is a bounded, crosschecked factual selection, not a bulk reproduction of their databases.
RSSSF author Peter Kungler permits copying with acknowledgement; his1939/40page supplies final table context, not per-match results.
Qualification games sometimes counted in both a cup and regional league. They appear once with a note rather than twice in historical totals.
Home and away are fixture designations; no relocated-ground matches were imported in this selection. AET is only supplied where documented.
Two Wolves opponent-index date discrepancies are resolved by the Wolves season-by-season pages, which agree with Albion Till We Die:25September1943 and26May1945. Retained in row sourceNote.

All 28 reported Football League South fixtures are represented once, including two dual-purpose Midland Cup games: seven crosschecked and 21 single-source records. Four single-source War Cup fixtures and two source-identified first-XI Birmingham & District League fixtures bring 1940/41 coverage to 34 records; 27 remain single-source. Regional league fixture coverage is complete against the cited season list, not independently verified in full.

The City Ground cites Brian McColl, Record of British Wartime Football; Ken Smales, The First 125 Years; and Albion Till We Die. Its provenance partly overlaps the Albion archive. Treat this as corroboration across compilations, not proof of wholly independent source lineage.

RSSSF, Peter Kungler, England 1940/41: Albion played 28 league games, won 13, drew 5, lost 10, goals 83–69. The aggregate includes 26 ordinary league fixtures and two Midland Cup games. Those dual-purpose games must appear once, not twice. URL: https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/eng41.html

The four Football League War Cup fixtures and two source-identified first-XI Birmingham & District League games are separate from the 28 regional league games. The District League identity is explicitly attributed to Albion Till We Die and awaits corroboration.
The 28 December 1940 Forest fixture was designated away but played at The Hawthorns. Home/away fields preserve the fixture designation; the public note explains the physical ground.

Contemporary newspaper checks did not yield further verified matches in this pass. Prince Albert Library requests returned HTTP 403; the cached February 22 text was insufficient. Six freely accessible Daily News issues had inadequate OCR. No score was inferred from unreadable text.

User approved clearly labelled single-source records on 19 October 2026. Such records have evidenceStatus single-source and no corroboration URL; they contribute only to the separate wartime totals. Reported tie aggregates are arithmetic from those same source scores, not independent verification.

Birmingham Daily Gazette, 13 January 1941, p. 2, Amateur’s Four Hat Tricks: public excerpt supports the Notts Midland Cup fixture at The Hawthorns and Richardson’s 250th goal, but omits the final score. Derby Daily Telegraph, 7 February 1941, p. 5, fixture excerpt is truncated after West Alb. v.; it cannot establish the Walsall match’s venue.

19 October 2026 league completion: added 19 Football League South and two source-identified first-XI District League results, all single-source. The 2 November 1940 Notts County fixture was designated away but played at The Hawthorns, following source footnote 1. Aggregate validation against RSSSF does not independently confirm individual scores.

1941/42: all 33 eligible physical fixtures from the cited season list represented, six retained crosschecked and 27 new single-source records. Thirteen first-phase league fixtures, 18 second-phase league fixtures (including nine qualifying and eight knockout cup games), and two source-identified first-XI District League games. Count each match once.

The nine cup qualifiers are included in the 18 second-phase league fixtures. All eight War Cup knockout games also counted in that league phase, including the four retained crosschecked Everton/Wolves games. Competition filters preserve the main cup classification; the page explains overlap.

RSSSF phase aggregates agree: first phase P13 W9 D1 L3 GF62 GA26; second P18 W9 D3 L6 GF53 GA43; cup qualifying P9 W4 D2 L3 GF29 GA24. Aggregate agreement is not independent match-level corroboration.

Walsall date uncertainty: source numeric date 23 May 1942 conflicts with its Monday label. Retain 23 May as explicitly source-reported, display the discrepancy and do not claim the date independently confirmed. Search found no confirming record; the Albion on-this-day May 23 URL returned 404.

The two Aston Villa District League fixtures are explicitly identified by the source as first-XI appearances in a competition usually played by Albion’s A team. Keep that identity qualification on each single-source row.

Friendlies on 1 November, 20 December, 28 March, 25 May and 30 May are excluded. The source repeats the 30 May friendly row; it is not an additional fixture. Scorers, attendances and source prose are not imported.

1942/43: all 38 physical fixtures from the cited season list represented, 12 crosschecked and 26 single-source records. Eighteen first-phase North league fixtures and 20 second-phase fixtures; all ten cup qualifiers and four knockout games also counted in the second league phase and appear once under their cup classification.

Both RSSSF league phase aggregates agree: first P18 W6 D4 L8 GF35 GA43; second P20 W11 D2 L7 GF49 GA40. All ten qualifier scores now have individual corroboration and sum to P10 W6 D0 L4 GF19 GA20. RSSSF’s qualifying table still lists GF19 GA22, which conflicts with the corroborated match record. No individual score was changed. Its full 54-team qualifying table totals GF1180/GA1182; that global imbalance alone does not locate every error. The archive retains the supported 19–20 total and discloses the external 19–22 reference conflict.
Reported War Cup ties: Albion beat Coventry 4–1 on aggregate, then lost 5–6 to Chesterfield. Tie arithmetic comes from the same single-source results; no extra-time claim is inferred.

Birmingham away fixtures on 5 December 1942, 6 February 1943 and 3 April 1943 were played at Villa Park according to the source. Home/away fields preserve designated away status and each public note explains the ground and air-raid damage.

All 38 listed fixture dates agree with the calendar weekdays. Repeated Chesterfield aggregate footnotes are not additional matches. No first-XI District League games or friendlies are listed on this season page; this is coverage against that cited list, not proof that no other informal football occurred. Scorers, attendances and source prose are not imported.

1943/44: all 39 eligible physical fixtures from the cited season list represented, eight retained crosschecked and 31 new single-source records. Eighteen first-phase North league fixtures and 21 second-phase fixtures; ten War Cup qualifiers and all ten Midland Cup games also counted in the second league phase and appear once under their cup classification.

RSSSF phase aggregates agree: first P18 W8 D3 L7 GF42 GA44; second P21 W5 D9 L7 GF46 GA48; War Cup qualifying P10 W2 D4 L4 GF24 GA29. The second-phase comparison uses the documented 2–2 regulation score for the 6 May final; the ledger retains the 4–3 cup score after extra time. The City Ground match page explicitly records both scores. Aggregate agreement is not independent match-level corroboration. Albion failed to qualify for the War Cup knockout stage.

The complete reported Midland Cup campaign is represented: four qualifying games, then two-legged ties against Walsall (Albion 3–2 aggregate), Stoke (Albion 4–2), and Forest (Albion 6–5 after extra time). The four newly added knockout scores remain single-source; both final legs retain their previous crosschecked evidence and extra-time status.

Date uncertainty: Birmingham City home follows 27 December 1943 in the season list, whose footnote reports alternative 26 December sources. Aston Villa away follows source numeric date 10 April 1944, although its Saturday label conflicts with calendar Monday. Both public rows disclose uncertainty; neither date is independently confirmed.

Four friendlies with mixed first/second-XI line-ups are excluded: Villa away 19 February, Villa XI home 25 March, Wolves XI home 1 April, Wolves XI away 15 April. They are not additional first-team competitive fixtures. No scorers, attendances or source prose are imported.

1944/45: all 40 fixtures from the cited season list represented, four retained crosschecked and 36 new single-source records. Eighteen first-phase North league fixtures and 22 second-phase fixtures; ten War Cup qualifiers and both two-legged cup ties also counted in the second league phase and appear once under their cup classification.

All three RSSSF aggregate comparisons agree: first P18 W9 D4 L5 GF36 GA30; second P22 W6 D7 L9 GF39 GA44; War Cup qualifying P10 W3 D4 L3 GF20 GA15. Aggregate agreement is not independent match-level corroboration.

Villa away on 26 December 1944 stopped after 81 minutes due to fog, but the source explicitly says the result was allowed to stand. Include its reported 4–3 score with a prominent single-source note; exclude interrupted matches without an accepted standing result. The same website’s Villa head-to-head is shared provenance, not corroboration.
Reported ties: Bristol City won 8–5 on aggregate in the War Cup first round; Leicester City won 3–1 in the Midland Cup. The Midland Cup round is not identified by the source and is not invented.

All 40 source fixture dates agree with calendar weekdays. No friendly or District League fixtures are listed in this season page; this does not assert no informal football occurred. Scorers, attendances and source prose are not imported.

1945/46 recovery season: all 42 Football League South fixtures from the cited list represented, 14 retained crosschecked and 28 new single-source records. This regional league continued wartime arrangements after the war; national league football resumed in 1946/47.

The complete fixture set totals P42 W22 D8 L12 GF104 GA69, agreeing with Greens on Screen’s season table (also matched by the Friardale season summary). Table agreement is not independent match-level corroboration. RSSSF’s England 1945/46 page does not supply this South table and is not cited as if it did.
Arsenal away on 12 January 1946 was played at White Hart Lane, Tottenham Hotspur’s ground. The fixture remains designated away, with the source footnote preserved as a public note.

The official FA Cup games against Cardiff on 5 and 9 January and Derby on 26 and 30 January remain solely in the competitive ledger. Three overseas tour games on 1, 4 and 8 May are excluded. No scorers, attendances or source prose are imported.
All listed league dates agree with calendar weekdays. All 21 opponents appear once home and once away; original 14 match records are unchanged.

1939/40: all 28 Midland Regional League fixtures from the cited source list are represented, eight retained crosschecked and 20 new single-source records. The six existing crosschecked War Cup fixtures remain separate, bringing the season to 34 physical matches.
The league set totals P28 W18 D4 L6 GF87 GA51, agreeing with RSSSF’s Midland regional table. Aggregate agreement does not independently corroborate individual dates, grounds or scores.

Birmingham away on 18 November 1939 and 24 February 1940 was played at The Hawthorns due to St Andrew’s safety closure; Northampton away on 5 June 1940 was also at The Hawthorns. Designated away status is preserved and public notes explain the physical venue.

Coventry away retains numeric date 8 June 1940, but the source weekday Wednesday conflicts with calendar Saturday. The discrepancy is visible in the row; date clarification remains pending. The prior research inventory also noted a Boxing Day 26/27 December lead; the source explicitly lists Tuesday 26 December and no second confirming date is claimed.

The three expunged national league matches remain only in the annulled appendix. Friendlies, mixed first/second XIs, and the fog-abandoned Sheffield Wednesday fixture without a stated standing result remain excluded. No scorers, attendances or source prose are imported.

pending.reason: All 28 listed Midland Regional League fixtures are now included: eight crosschecked plus 20 labelled single-source additions in wartime-1939-40-research.json. Further match-level corroboration remains outstanding. Coventry’s 8 June weekday discrepancy is disclosed; the source lists Boxing Day as 26 December, without a second confirming date being claimed.
